pŭtātīvus , a, um, adj. id.,
I.imaginary, presumptive, putative (post-class.): “habitus, actus,” Tert. adv. Marc. 3, 8 : “caro Christi,” id. Carn. Chr. 1 : magister, Vet. Interp. Iren. 4, 60.—Adv.: pŭtātīvē , by supposition, putatively, Hier. adv. Joann. Hierosol. 24: natus, Hilar. Trin. 6, 5.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
